\section{Gaussian Space --- Product Bounds}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProductBounds
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Product Bounds: Introduction}
First and second coordinate Gaussian derivative kernels admit integrable quadratic majorants. Their expectations give global bounds in terms of the common variance.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Product Bounds: Results}

\begin{lemma}[First coordinate Gaussian score bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianCoordinate_first_kernel_integrable_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_j)_{j\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $v>0$. Equip
$\mathbb R^I$ with the product Gaussian measure whose coordinate at $j$ has mean $c_j$
and variance parameter $v$. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and satisfies
$|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$, then for each $i\in I$ the function $z\mapsto
((z_i-c_i)/v)f(z)$ is integrable, and its integral has absolute value at most $1+1/v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic majorant for a Hessian score]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_productHessian_mul_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\iota$ be a set, let $c,z\colon\iota\to\mathbb R$, and let $v>0$. For any
$i,j\in\iota$ and any $a\in\mathbb R$ with $|a|\le1$, one has
\[\left|\left(\frac{(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)}{v^2}-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{v}\right)a\right|\le\frac{(z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2}{2v^2}+\frac1v,\]
where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a Gaussian quadratic bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\difficulty{1}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, let $v\ge 0$, and let $i,j\in I$. The
function $z\mapsto\bigl((z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2\bigr)/(2v^2)+1/v$ is integrable under
the product measure whose $k$th coordinate has Gaussian law with mean $c_k$ and variance
$v$; at $v=0$, the quotients are interpreted using the usual convention that division by
zero is zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Integral of a Quadratic Expression]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_productHessian_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite type, let $c:I\to\mathbb R$, and let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$. For any
$i,j\in I$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb
R^I}\left(\frac{(z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2}{2v^2}+\frac1v\right)\,d\Bigl(\bigotimes_{k\in
I}N(c_k,v)\Bigr)(z)=\frac2v,
\]
where each $N(c_k,v)$ is a Gaussian measure with mean $c_k$ and variance parameter $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of Gaussian Hessian products]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_productHessian_mul_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_bound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $v>0$. If $f:\mathbb
R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and satisfies $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z$, then for every
$i,j\in I$ the function
\[z\longmapsto \left(\frac{(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)}{v^2}-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{v}\right)f(z)
\]
is integrable under the product Gaussian measure with independent coordinates of means
$c_k$ and variance parameter $v$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Product Gaussian Hessian integral bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_productHessian_mul_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_productHessian_mul_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_productHessian_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $v$ be a nonzero nonnegative
real number. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. For any
$i,j\in I$, under the product of Gaussian measures with means $c_k$ and common variance
$v$, \[\left|\int_{\mathbb
R^I}\left(\frac{(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)}{v^2}-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{v}\right)f(z)\,d\mu(z)\right|\le\frac2v,\]
where $\delta_{ij}=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}
